texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Q: Do you have any advice on running a recurring PM team meeting? My startup has recently grown to four PMs and I feel us getting slowly out of sync since so much more is going on now.
texts.text: Q: Do you have any advice on running a recurring PM team meeting? My startup has recently grown to four PMs and I feel us getting slowly out of sync since so much more is going on now.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Image from Leading a PM team meeting - Issue 19
texts.text: Image from Leading a PM team meeting - Issue 19

texts.label: text
texts.orig: I decided to tackle this question this week because during these turbulent times it’s especially important to strengthen the bonds between you and your teammates.
texts.text: I decided to tackle this question this week because during these turbulent times it’s especially important to strengthen the bonds between you and your teammates.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: PM team meetings can be one of your most fun and valuable meetings, getting everyone aligned and energized, but they can also easily be your most painful. I’ve heard stories of a PM team meeting (at a company that will go unnamed) where each week a PM presented her plans to the PM team, who then competed for how much they could tear that plan apart. 🤮
texts.text: PM team meetings can be one of your most fun and valuable meetings, getting everyone aligned and energized, but they can also easily be your most painful. I’ve heard stories of a PM team meeting (at a company that will go unnamed) where each week a PM presented her plans to the PM team, who then competed for how much they could tear that plan apart. 🤮

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Let’s avoid that.
texts.text: Let’s avoid that.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: My top five tips for leading effective PM team meetings:
texts.text: My top five tips for leading effective PM team meetings:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 1. Do you even need a PM team meeting?
texts.text: 1. Do you even need a PM team meeting?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Don’t do this meeting just to do it. Make certain that adding (or continuing this meeting) is consistently worth everyone’s time. What problem are you trying to solve? Actually write this out. Are there more efficient ways to solve this problem?
texts.text: Don’t do this meeting just to do it. Make certain that adding (or continuing this meeting) is consistently worth everyone’s time. What problem are you trying to solve? Actually write this out. Are there more efficient ways to solve this problem?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 2. Be crystal clear on the goal
texts.text: 2. Be crystal clear on the goal

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Again, it’s important that you have a clear goal for this meeting, and that you regularly check-in with yourself and your teammates on how you’re doing.
texts.text: Again, it’s important that you have a clear goal for this meeting, and that you regularly check-in with yourself and your teammates on how you’re doing.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The three typical goals for this meeting:
texts.text: The three typical goals for this meeting:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Understanding: Make sure everyone feels like they know what’s going on, inside, and outside the team.
texts.text: Understanding: Make sure everyone feels like they know what’s going on, inside, and outside the team.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Alignment: Make sure everyone on the team is aligned.
texts.text: Alignment: Make sure everyone on the team is aligned.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Connection: Tighten the bonds between everyone on your team.
texts.text: Connection: Tighten the bonds between everyone on your team.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If there are other goals, great. If it’s just a single goal, even better. Make these goals explicit when creating the meeting, and continue to check-in on whether you’re achieving these goals.
texts.text: If there are other goals, great. If it’s just a single goal, even better. Make these goals explicit when creating the meeting, and continue to check-in on whether you’re achieving these goals.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 3. Meet often enough, but not too often
texts.text: 3. Meet often enough, but not too often

texts.label: text
texts.orig: I’d suggest one to two times a month. The bigger the team, the less frequent. A weekly PM team meeting becomes redundant with your 1:1’s. Meeting less than monthly can be valuable for social/bonding purposes, but most of the other benefits go away. Also, no laptops allowed.
texts.text: I’d suggest one to two times a month. The bigger the team, the less frequent. A weekly PM team meeting becomes redundant with your 1:1’s. Meeting less than monthly can be valuable for social/bonding purposes, but most of the other benefits go away. Also, no laptops allowed.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 4. Make it easy to find, and to add to, the meeting agenda
texts.text: 4. Make it easy to find, and to add to, the meeting agenda

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Put the agenda for each meeting into a shared Google doc (or whatever document platform you prefer), and link to it in the invite. As new items come up throughout the week, add to this doc. You want your team to be able to see what’s planned ahead of each meeting.
texts.text: Put the agenda for each meeting into a shared Google doc (or whatever document platform you prefer), and link to it in the invite. As new items come up throughout the week, add to this doc. You want your team to be able to see what’s planned ahead of each meeting.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A typical PM meeting agenda:
texts.text: A typical PM meeting agenda:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Manager shares useful information: What’s important for the team to know about what’s happening inside and outside of the team, upcoming changes to the team, and updates on planning timelines, etc.
texts.text: Manager shares useful information: What’s important for the team to know about what’s happening inside and outside of the team, upcoming changes to the team, and updates on planning timelines, etc.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: ICs share useful information: Upcoming launches, process changes, learnings, etc.
texts.text: ICs share useful information: Upcoming launches, process changes, learnings, etc.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Q&A
texts.text: Q&A

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If you’re a small team, I would suggest letting anyone on the team directly add items to the agenda doc. If you’re a large team (e.g bigger than say a dozen people), have someone be the point person for each meeting’s agenda.
texts.text: If you’re a small team, I would suggest letting anyone on the team directly add items to the agenda doc. If you’re a large team (e.g bigger than say a dozen people), have someone be the point person for each meeting’s agenda.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 5. Make it fun
texts.text: 5. Make it fun

texts.label: text
texts.orig: PM team meetings tend to get super serious. Find ways to add a bit of joy and lightheartedness to the meetings. A few suggestions:
texts.text: PM team meetings tend to get super serious. Find ways to add a bit of joy and lightheartedness to the meetings. A few suggestions:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Have each person share something fun they did recently
texts.text: Have each person share something fun they did recently

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Invite guest speakers
texts.text: Invite guest speakers

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Do a book club
texts.text: Do a book club

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Have the meeting in an interesting location (once we’re allowed to)
texts.text: Have the meeting in an interesting location (once we’re allowed to)

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Go out for drinks afterward (once we’re allowed to)
texts.text: Go out for drinks afterward (once we’re allowed to)

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Give these tips a shot and let me know how it goes. And if you have any other tips to share, I’d love to hear them.
